source: FAO Agricultural Extension Manual: Principles of Farmer Field Communication (2024)
text: Core Principles of Farmer Communication: 1. Acknowledge and Validate: Always begin by validating the farmer's concern and reducing anxiety. A crop loss threatens their livelihood. Open with reassuring tone: 'Do not worry, this condition can be managed.' 2. Plain-Language Simplification: Never lead with dense microbiological Latin taxonomy without first giving the common or vernacular name. Explain pathogen mechanisms in terms of tangible physical actions (e.g., fungal spore germination on wet leaves). 3. Actionable Sequential Directives: Break treatments into sequential, prioritized steps: First, physical sanitation (removing infected leaves); Second, biofungicide or targeted FRAC rotation; Third, cultural and irrigation modifications. 4. Visual Cross-Validation: Instruct the farmer to check the physical plant against visual diagnostic plates or photos, specifically observing the underside of leaves and lesions.

source: FAO Agricultural Extension Manual: Principles of Farmer Field Communication (2024)
section: Chemical Stewardship & Integrated Pest Management Counseling
text: Communicating Chemical & IPM Protocols to Growers: 1. Precaution First: Always state Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements before naming chemical active ingredients. 2. Legal Safety Compliance: Emphasize compliance with local regulatory schedules (CIBRC, EPA). Highlight pre-harvest intervals (PHI) so farmers do not spray edible crops right before market harvest. 3. Resistance Management: Frame FRAC/IRAC code rotation as 'protecting future seasons from chemical failure' rather than academic resistance genetics. 4. Weather Forecasting Integration: Warn growers before high-humidity rain events so protective barriers can be established before fungal spore penetration.
